title: A New Flat in Dunford
passage: Hi Ana, I'm writing from my new flat in Dunford! I moved here last Saturday with my brother, and we carried all the boxes up three floors because there is no lift. My legs are still tired, but I love the flat. It has a big window in the kitchen and a small balcony.

The town is quiet, and the people are friendly. There is a bakery next door, and the owner gave me a free bread roll on my first morning. My new job at the library starts on Monday. The bus ride takes twenty minutes, so I have to get up at seven.

I'm a little nervous about the job, but I think I'll be fine. Why don't you come and visit in two weeks? You can sleep on the sofa, and I'll cook your favourite pasta. Please write back soon! Love, Marta

title: The Vegetable Stall on Mill Street
passage: Every Saturday morning, Rosa Vega opens her small stall in the market on Mill Street. She gets up at four o'clock, because she has to drive to her farm and collect the vegetables. By eight o'clock, the stall is full of tomatoes, carrots and green beans, and the first customers are already there.

Rosa's vegetables are not the cheapest in town. Tomatoes are cheaper in the supermarket. But many people prefer her stall, because her vegetables are fresh and she always has time to talk. "I know all my customers," she says. "I know who likes big carrots and who has a new baby."

Rosa goes home at two o'clock, very tired. She says the work is hard, but she loves being outside all day. Next spring, she is going to open a second stall in the next town, and her son will help her there. "I want him to learn about the farm," she says.
